The Guardian (UK news) — datePublished 2026-10-25T17:10:11Z = 17:10 GMT Sun 25 Oct (after the 01:00Z BST/GMT cutover, so Z = local). dateModified 2026-10-25T17:31:46Z = 17:31 GMT. Guardian's own byline furniture says "First published on Sun 25 Oct 2026 10.03 GMT". Retrieved by curl at 17:32 GMT.

HEADLINE: "One dead and 82,000 properties without power as Storm Boelo batters UK"
STANDFIRST: "Man, 60, killed by falling tree near Castle Douglas in Scotland as Met Office reports gusts of up to 84mph"
BYLINE: Hannah Al-Othman, North of England correspondent

THE DEATH
"A 60-year-old man has been killed by a falling tree and more than 82,000 properties have been left without power as Storm Boelo continues to batter Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England."
Police Scotland spokesperson, quoted directly: "We were made aware of a 60-year-old man having been struck by a falling tree on a minor road at Mid Kelton around 10.30am on Sunday, 25 October, 2026." / "The man was pronounced dead at the scene. There are no suspicious circumstances and a report will be submitted to the procurator fiscal in due course."
Guardian says Police Scotland "revealed that a man had died on Sunday morning".

POWER — AS CARRIED BY THE GUARDIAN
"Engineers had restored power to 344,900 customers but 82,6000 remained disconnected, the Energy Networks Association (ENA) said on Sunday morning. The figure included more than 30,000 homes across Scotland." [NOTE: "82,6000" is a literal typo in the Guardian copy; the figure is 82,600 as carried by BBC and the Independent.]
ENA statement: "The networks have been focused on reconnecting customers this morning, though the continuing severe weather in some regions is limiting network engineers' opportunities to safely start the work of restoring customers' power today and access to certain areas remains difficult. Engineers are working around the clock to identify and fix faults."
Separately and later in the same piece: "Around 53,000 homes in Scotland were still without power by 5pm on Sunday, according to updates from SP Energy Networks and Scottish and Southern Electricity Networks (SSEN)."

GUSTS — AS CARRIED BY THE GUARDIAN (attributed to the Met Office)
Winds "widely reached 60-70mph". Tiree, Inner Hebrides 82mph. Argyll and Bute 84mph. Snowdonia (Eryri) 83mph.

WARNING TIMINGS
Amber warning "came into force at 9pm on Saturday", covering Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and the far north of England.

FLOODING
"The Environment Agency had issued six warnings as of 1.45pm that flooding was expected for spots in northern parts of England, as well as 50 alerts stating flooding was possible. The Scottish Environment Protection Agency said 17 flood warnings and 11 flooding alerts were active as of the same time."

OTHER
Scottish government's Resilience Room met Sunday afternoon on outages and restoration.
Met Office chief forecaster Jason Kelly, quoted: "Storm Boelo will be felt across the UK this weekend, with the strongest winds and greatest potential for disruption in the north. Amber warnings are in place across mainland Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and the far north of England, where gusts of 60-70mph are expected widely, with the potential for 80mph in exposed coastal locations."
Cancellations: Liverpool's River of Light; London's Diwali on the Square; Edinburgh Castle closed Sunday; Fountains Abbey estate, North Yorkshire, closed.
Cumbria police took overnight calls on localised flooding and fallen trees.
Storm Austen (Friday, south-west England): 76mph St Mary's airport, Isles of Scilly; 74mph Aberporth, south Wales; 71mph Culdrose, Cornwall. Hundreds of homes still off in the south-west.
